children: The Bank of Mexico stays on hold as expected but omits from its statement that it expects to leave interest rates at their current level, while adding that it wouldn't necessarily react to further moves by the Federal Reserve. "This new statement gives the bank some wiggle room to move in either direction, especially given its explicit note that it would not 'react mechanically' to the anticipated adjustments to the federal funds rate," Rabobank's Molly Schwartz and Christian Lawrence say in a note. "We believe Banxico will maintain the overnight policy rate at 6.5% going forward, though the risk is skewed in favor of a hike." (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
